date_note: Cybersecurity.com (24 November) says the unauthorized access happened on 18 November and that JAXA announced it on 24 November.
title: JAXA says unauthorized access to its public Earth-observation data system exposed account data of 2,000 users
summary: Cybersecurity.com reports that JAXA announced on 24 November that its public information system, which provides precipitation and weather data, was accessed without authorization on 18 November. According to that report, account names and encrypted passwords of 2,000 users were leaked. JAXA is said to have cut the web server off the network and says it is investigating; the cause and full scope are still under investigation.
plain: Japan's space agency JAXA says an outsider got into its public data system on 18 November; per the report, account names and encrypted passwords of 2,000 users leaked and the system was taken offline.
exec: A national space agency's public data service leaked account credentials of 2,000 users, per Cybersecurity.com's account of JAXA's announcement.
action: General advice: users of the JAXA service who reused that password elsewhere should change it; the page's editors also advise operators to hash stored passwords with salt.
